theory_content: Whether a holding can hurt you is decided by its size, not by how good the idea was. A speculative position at 2% of the portfolio that goes to zero costs 2%; the same idea at 40% ends the portfolio. Professional risk management is mostly about sizing, and amateurs almost always focus on selection instead.

theory_title: Measuring how lopsided a portfolio is
theory_content: The Herfindahl index adds the squared weights of every holding: a portfolio split evenly across ten names scores 0.1, while one with 70% in a single stock scores over 0.5. It captures what a list of holdings hides — that "twelve stocks" can still be one bet if one of them is most of the money.

theory_title: Diversification that only looks like diversification
theory_content: Four IT companies are four names and one bet, because they rise and fall together. What reduces risk is holding things that respond to different drivers — sectors, geographies, and asset classes. In a genuine crash correlations rise towards one, which is exactly when diversification is needed and least available.

theory_title: Selling what ran, buying what lagged
theory_content: Set a target allocation, then restore it on a schedule or when a band is breached — say 5 percentage points. After a strong equity year this forces you to sell equity and buy debt, which feels wrong and is the point: it mechanically sells high and buys low without requiring a forecast.
